title: Defeat of the Ammonites and Syrians

questions.question: Why did David send messengers to Hanun king of the Ammonites?
options: To console him concerning his father
questions.correctAnswer: To console him concerning his father
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:2 (ESV): "...I will deal loyally with Hanun... So David sent messengers to console him concerning his father."

questions.question: What did the princes of Ammon persuade Hanun to believe?
options: That David sent spies to search and overthrow the land
That David wanted to marry his daughter
questions.correctAnswer: That David sent spies to search and overthrow the land
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:3 (ESV): "...Has not David sent his servants to you to search and to overthrow and to spy out the land?"

questions.question: How did Hanun treat David’s servants?
options: He shaved them and cut off their garments in the middle
questions.correctAnswer: He shaved them and cut off their garments in the middle
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:4 (ESV): "...shaved them and cut off their garments in the middle, at their hips, and sent them away."

questions.question: Where did David tell his men to stay until their beards grew?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:5 (ESV): "...Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown and then return."

questions.question: Who did the Ammonites hire to help them against David?
options: The Syrians (Arameans) of Mesopotamia and others
questions.correctAnswer: The Syrians (Arameans) of Mesopotamia and others
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:6 (ESV): "...to hire chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, from Aram-maacah, and from Zobah."

questions.question: Who led the army of Israel?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:8 (ESV): "...he sent Joab and all the host of the mighty men."

questions.question: How did Joab divide his forces?
options: He took the best men to fight the Syrians and left the rest with Abishai to fight the Ammonites
questions.correctAnswer: He took the best men to fight the Syrians and left the rest with Abishai to fight the Ammonites
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:10-11 (ESV): "...he selected all the choice men of Israel... The rest of the troops he put in the charge of Abishai his brother..."

questions.question: What agreement did Joab make with Abishai?
options: If the Syrians are too strong for me, you help me; if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I help you
questions.correctAnswer: If the Syrians are too strong for me, you help me; if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I help you
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:12 (ESV): "If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me..."

questions.question: What did the Ammonites do when they saw the Syrians fled?
options: They also fled before Abishai and entered the city
questions.correctAnswer: They also fled before Abishai and entered the city
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:15 (ESV): "And when the Ammonites saw that the Syrians fled, they likewise fled before Abishai his brother and entered the city."

questions.question: How many talents of silver did the Ammonites send to hire chariots?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:6 (ESV): "...sent 1,000 talents of silver to hire chariots..."

questions.question: How many chariots did they hire?
Who was the commander of the army of Hadadezer?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:16 (ESV): "...and Shophach the commander of the army of Hadadezer was at their head."

questions.question: How many Syrians did David kill in the second battle?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:18 (ESV): "...David killed of the Syrians the men of 7,000 chariots and 40,000 foot soldiers..."

questions.question: What was the result of the war for the servants of Hadadezer?
options: They made peace with David and became subject to him
questions.correctAnswer: They made peace with David and became subject to him
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 19:19 (ESV): "...they made peace with David and became subject to him..."

key_verse_text: Be strong, and let us use our strength for our people and for the cities of our God, and may the LORD do what seems good to him.
